description: key-hierarchy design §5.6 (the simple fork rule): trees of verified epochs (labels stand for their UTF-8 bytes; each node carries its recovery fingerprint), what the device brings (its pinned chain, its stored answers per branch, rejected authors), and the expected chain, open questions (per side, the authors still to answer for; the suggested default; conflicting resolves), the branches it must settle with its own resolve, the re-application set, and the resolves it followed. The attack trees of the earlier review rounds end in "no effect" or "one question".

cases.name: honest concurrent removals: A, pinned on its side, is asked about B's side only
honest concurrent removals: A answers yes to B, keeps its side, and re-applies Y in its resolve
honest concurrent removals: an unpinned joiner asks at the branch and waits
rule 4: a joiner follows the resolve settling the branch at epoch 1
rule 4(b): B, pinned on its own side, follows A's resolve on the other side
rule 4: C, pinned on the resolve's side, takes it as settling the branch
amendment 4: a question on the pinned chain does not stop linear following
rule 4(c): two resolves for different sides: the joiner is asked, with both
amendment 2: after "yes" to B's removal of Y, Y's epoch on the chosen side is not followed
amendment 2: Y's epoch from before its removal on the chosen side is kept
rule 4(b): B, pinned on a stale side that removed X, follows C's resolve through X's earlier epoch
a side vouched by a resolve after the answer is asked about again
an attacker's resolve that is itself a child of the branch settles nothing: the island device is asked
rule 6: an author rejected in an answer is ignored everywhere
round 1 C1: pinned through the removal of X, A is asked about B's change only (X ignored)
round 1 C1: A answers yes to B; Y is already removed, nothing to re-apply
round 1 C1: an unpinned joiner asks once at epoch 1 (B then X; A then C)
round 1 C1: the joiner answers truthfully
round 2 deadlock tree: pinned through m2, C is asked about B's change only
round 2 deadlock tree: an unpinned joiner asks once
round 2 child tree: pinned through m2, X's fork has no effect
round 2 child tree: an unpinned joiner asks once
round 3 H1 (D removes X under X's fork): pinned, asked about B only; no permanent dispute
round 3 H1 (D): after "yes" to B, settled
round 3 H1 (P removes X under X's fork): pinned, asked about B only; no permanent dispute
round 3 H1 (P): after "yes" to B, settled
round 3 H2 (X's legitimate epoch, its fork, D under it): pinned on the real chain, no effect
round 3 H2: an unpinned joiner follows e2 linearly and asks at e2
round 3 H2: the joiner answers truthfully: D's removal of X is confirmed, X rejected
X removed every resolver: a joiner cannot follow C's resolve and is asked
X removed every resolver: a device pinned through 2a is unaffected
a puppet's resolve on X's side is never followed (X, on its path, is removed): one question
a puppet rejected in an answer is ignored, and X with it
